subject: Post-call: align on throughput & schedule dedicated sizing call for Starlane
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@starlane.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 May 2025 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: align on throughput & schedule dedicated sizing call for Starlane

Hi Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned:

- What we heard: P1 is real-time document summarization in the product (avg doc length ~6k tokens) with peak concurrent users ~120 and 95th pct latency target <= 300ms for short completions (100–200 tokens).
- What matters next: a dedicated capacity sizing session where we map your traffic shape (seq length distribution, concurrency patterns), confirm KV/prefix caching strategy, and pick an initial dedicated GPU profile.

Proposed times for a 60–75 minute sizing deep-dive (we'll bring an infra engineer + runtime lead):
- Thu May 8 — 09:30–10:45 PT
- Thu May 8 — 13:00–14:15 PT
- Fri May 9 — 10:00–11:15 PT

If none of those work, tell me three slots that do and we’ll lock one. I attached a short sizing checklist that will speed the call (workload snapshot, sample logs, and token distribution).

Next steps from our side once time is locked: share a mutual action plan (MAP) and a pre-call questionnaire. Grace/Ben — I looped you to prep the checklist and the MAP draft; Ben can we have a starter MAP by EOD Wed?

Thanks,
Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0191
[Attachment: sizing-checklist.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)]

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@starlane.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@starlane.ai
Date: Tue, 6 May 2025 17:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: align on throughput & schedule dedicated sizing call for Starlane

On Tue, May 6, 2025 at 3:04 PM -0700, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Alex — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we stay aligned:
> 
> - What we heard: P1 is real-time document summarization in the product (avg doc length ~6k tokens) with peak concurrent users ~120 and 95th pct latency target <= 300ms for short completions (100–200 tokens).

Thanks Rafael — this is helpful. Thu May 8 09:30 PT works for our Lead Eng (Isha) and me. A couple of things for the agenda so your team can prep:

- We’ll share a short traffic sample and one anonymized log file ahead of time — will that be sufficient to approximate KV cache hit rates?
- Can you confirm whether Redwood's dedicated pools support persistent KV caches across requests (we’re worried about warmup cost on cold-starts)?
- We also need to include a short procurement checkpoint — procurement@starlane.ai is CC'd. They may want to join the first 15m for license/pricing framing and then drop if needed.

If you can send the MAP and pre-call questionnaire today/tonight, we’ll complete the questionnaire and upload the sample by tomorrow morning.

Alex
Director of AI Products | Starlane AI
alex.turner@starlane.ai | +1 (212) 555-0134

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 May 2025 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: align on throughput & schedule dedicated sizing call for Starlane — prep items
Grace/Ben — forwarding Alex's note. Action items below so we can move quickly:
1) Ben: finalize the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft and the pre-call questionnaire attached to this thread. Keep the questionnaire focused (traffic snapshot, sample logs, desired SLOs, token distribution). Aim for a single page.
2) Grace: prepare a short deck (4 slides) that explains Redwood Dedicated options, cache behavior (prefix/KV caching), and our typical latency profile for summarization workloads. Include a one-slide recommended starting configuration for their expected concurrency and average seq length.
3) Ops: confirm whether we have an example of persistent KV cache behavior for cross-request warm starts we can share — if there's a short note or an internal runbook, link it.
I attached the sizing checklist again and a MAP skeleton — Ben, please add pricing checkpoint language for procurement. 
Timing: Alex said Thu May 8 09:30 PT works. Can we confirm availability for you both? If yes, I’ll send the calendar invite and the MAP + questionnaire tonight.
Thanks — Rafael

[Attachment: mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf (PDF, 92KB)]

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@starlane.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, procurement@starlane.ai
Date: Thu, 8 May 2025 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: align on throughput & schedule dedicated sizing call for Starlane

Alex — confirmed and calendar invite sent for Thu May 8 09:30–10:45 PT (Google Meet link below). Thanks for flagging procurement; we’ll reserve the first 15 minutes for pricing and then transition to the technical deep-dive.
Prep pack (links/attachments):
- MAP (attached): mutual-action-plan-v1.pdf
- Sizing checklist (attached): sizing-checklist.xlsx
- Pre-call Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AStarlane-Shared-Docs
Quick answers to Alex's questions:
- A traffic sample + one anonymized log is sufficient to approximate cache hit rates for a first-pass estimate. We’ll use it to model expected KV hit-rate and warmup impact.
- Redwood Dedicated supports workload-aware KV/prefix caching strategies. We have options for sticky caches vs. ephemeral caches; we’ll review pros/cons during the call and show a warmup mitigation pattern.
If anything changes on timing, reply-all and we’ll adjust. Looking forward — Rafael
Google Meet: https://meet.google.com/abc-defg-hij
--
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
